tickets.title: Mechanical decision-contract validator (partition + rank + lede-rationale) with unit tests + fixture reconciliation
tickets.context:
[DONE — see .ailoop/evidence/T001.txt. Added DecisionContractError + validateDecisionContract(decision,entries) (partition+rank, pre-assemble) + validateLedeRationale(resume) (post-assemble) to validate.ts, NOT wired. Reconciliation: NO loosening — strict 'every full-rephrase-section lede' holds because all 3 cloudcase-* seed experience entries share one groupBy key -> one group/fixture. validateLedeRationale takes only (resume).] Lede is a self-hosted resume-tailoring tool. The tailoring engine is a single structured LLM call returning FLAT judgment `TailorDecision` = { signals:{roleLevel,weights[],hardRequirements[]}, summary, items:[{entryId,text,rank:number,leadRationale?}], cut:[{entryId,reason}] } (schema `src/shared/schema.ts` `TailorDecisionZ`). The server assembles all structure (`src/server/tailor/assemble.ts`) and already mechanically rejects fabricated NUMBERS (`validateNoFabrication` + `class FabricationError` in `src/server/tailor/validate.ts`). LOCKED (cite oracle.md): the model returns judgment only; NO LLM-checks-LLM (this validator is pure mechanical, no model call); recorded fixtures in `test/fixtures/decisions/*.json` are captured real model output and are NEVER edited. SYSTEM_PROMPT frozen — do not touch prompt.ts.

BUILD ONLY THIS: a NEW mechanical validator in `src/server/tailor/validate.ts`, sibling to `validateNoFabrication` — add `class DecisionContractError extends Error` (name it, like FabricationError) and `export function validateDecisionContract(...)`. Do NOT wire it into tailor() or the route here — that is T002. Do NOT tighten `TailorDecisionZ` (the rank check needs a library lookup zod can't do; keep it in this validator).

The validator enforces THREE invariants over the flat `TailorDecision` + the `Entry[]` library (each Entry has `.id` and `.section`):
1. PARTITION (on the raw decision, pre-assemble): the library's entry-id set === entryIds(items) ∪ entryIds(cut) EXACTLY; items/cut disjoint; no library entry omitted from both; no id in both lists; no id in items or cut absent from the library (foreign ids rejected); no id appearing twice within items or within cut.
2. RANK (on the raw decision, pre-assemble): each item.rank is an INTEGER >= 1, unique WITHIN its section — where an item's section is resolved by looking its entryId up in the library (`entry.section`); the raw decision has no section field. Equal ranks in the SAME section → reject; equal ranks in DIFFERENT sections → fine (each section leads with a rank-1).
3. LEDE RATIONALE (post-assemble — needs the assembled `TailoredResume` from `assemble()` because grouping determines ledes): every lede in a `rephrase:"full"` section (experience, project — read `rephrase` from `SECTIONS` in `src/shared/sections.ts`) carries a non-empty (trimmed, non-blank) `leadRationale`. A lede is the lowest-rank item within a group; `assemble` already exposes each group's lede rationale as `group.leadRationale` (assemble.ts:129, items ordered rank-asc so items[0] is the lede). Extra `leadRationale` on a NON-lede item is TOLERATED and discarded (current assemble behavior) — do NOT reject it.

Expose the shape so both raw-decision checks (partition, rank) and the post-assemble check (lede rationale) are callable — e.g. `validateDecisionContract(decision, entries)` for the flat checks and a `validateLedeRationale(resume, entries)` (or accept both) — T002 will call the flat part before assemble and the lede part after. Match `validateNoFabrication`'s throw style (typed error, descriptive message).

FIXTURE RECONCILIATION (the whole reason P0 is first — do this and report the outcome): run your validator over ALL recorded fixtures in `test/fixtures/decisions/*.json` by feeding each `decision` through the REAL `assemble(decision, entries, layout, SECTIONS)` (use `SEED_ENTRIES`/seed library from `src/server/seed.ts` — the fixtures were recorded against it; hashKey in evalcore.ts confirms entries-only keying) and then validating. Each recorded fixture has only ~1 `leadRationale` across 2-3 items (platform-sdk: 2 items/1 rationale; rules-engine: 3/1; frontend-rewrite: 2/1). If a full-rephrase-section fixture has MULTIPLE full-section groups but only one rationale, the 'every full-section lede' scope will REJECT a real recorded decision — that is evidence the invariant is MIS-SCOPED. Per spec Fixture reconciliation: LOOSEN the invariant (e.g. scope to whatever the recorded fixtures empirically satisfy) — do NOT edit the fixture. Document the FINAL lede-rationale scope you landed on (and why) in a comment + return it to the coordinator so oracle.md can be updated. The partition/rank invariants must ALSO pass all fixtures.
tickets.acceptance:
- `bun run check` exit 0; `bunx vitest run` all pass (full suite — the wired-in keyless suite is unaffected yet since T001 does not wire).
- NEW `test/decision-contract.test.ts` with contrast cases (input->output, not existence). RED-TEAM-sharpened:
  - Partition: omit a library entry from both lists -> throws; exact partition -> passes; id in BOTH items and cut -> throws; id in exactly one -> passes; a FOREIGN id absent from the library but realistically SHAPED like a real id (e.g. borrowed from a different seed library, NOT 'zzz-nonexistent' — rules out format-sniffing) -> throws; the SAME id appearing TWICE within items (partition otherwise exact) -> throws AS A DISTINCT CASE from the both-lists case; the same id twice within cut -> throws. (These are multiset checks — a set-size comparison that masks a dup must fail.)
  - Rank: two items SAME section equal rank -> throws AND the thrown error message names the section + rank + colliding ids; the SAME rank value repeated across 3+ DIFFERENT sections -> passes (a global-uniqueness impl fails this — proves per-section resolution actually ran); non-integer rank 1.5 -> throws; rank NaN -> throws; rank Infinity -> throws; rank as string '1' -> throws; rank 0 / < 1 -> throws; unique integer ranks -> passes.
  - Lede rationale: a full-rephrase-section group whose lowest-rank item has empty/whitespace/missing leadRationale -> throws; full-section lede with non-blank rationale -> passes; **HIGH-VALUE: a group whose lowest-rank item is NOT first in the raw `items` array (out-of-order input) -> the rationale requirement follows RANK/assembled-lede, not array position** (a builder reading 'lede'='items[0] in decision order' fails this); a NON-lede item MISSING its rationale in a full-rephrase section -> does NOT throw (proves scoped to ledes, not every item — guards over-eager 'require on all'); a lede in a light/none section (education/skill) with NO rationale -> passes (proves scoping).
  - Fixture reconciliation: a test that runs validateDecisionContract over every recorded fixture (via real assemble + seed entries) and asserts NONE throw; AND asserts a NON-ZERO count of actually-checked full-rephrase-section ledes across the fixture set (so a scope loosened to near-vacuous — 'check nothing' — fails this count assertion, forcing any loosening to stay minimal and VISIBLE in test output, not buried in prose). If reconciliation forced a loosening, the test documents the final scope.
- Report to coordinator: the FINAL lede-rationale scope (unchanged 'every full-section lede', or loosened — and to what, with the fixture evidence AND the checked-lede count).

tickets.title: Wire validateDecisionContract into tailor() + map DecisionContractError to a distinct HTTP code with current-untouched persistence
tickets.origin: spec Deliverable 1 (placement + failure mode + route) + Phase 0
tickets.context:
Depends on T001, which built `validateDecisionContract` + `class DecisionContractError` in `src/server/tailor/validate.ts` (its final lede-rationale scope is whatever T001 reconciled to — you do NOT re-decide it; just call it). LOCKED (oracle.md): no LLM-checks-LLM; no self-repair/re-prompt; recorded fixtures never edited; SYSTEM_PROMPT frozen.

BUILD ONLY THIS — the WIRING:
1. In `src/server/tailor/engine.ts` `tailor()` (currently: decide -> assemble -> validateNoFabrication -> return): insert the contract checks so PLACEMENT mirrors fabrication exactly — the flat checks (partition, rank) run on the RAW `decision` BEFORE `assemble`; the lede-rationale check runs POST-assemble (on the `resume`). Both inside `tailor()`, OUTSIDE the provider retry envelope (the retry lives inside `ProviderEngine.decide`; `tailor()` is already outside it — do not add any retry). A violation throws `DecisionContractError`, NO self-repair, NO extra model retry.
2. In `src/server/routes/applications.ts` `mapTailorError` (line ~92 — the SINGLE copy; the 'index.ts' mention in its comment is stale, grep confirms no other): add a branch mapping `DecisionContractError` to its OWN HTTP status, DISTINCT from the fabrication 502 (`FabricationError` -> 502) and from NoFixtureError's 422. Pick a sensible distinct code + a distinct `error` string (ambient default — do not add a config knob). Import `DecisionContractError` from `../tailor/validate`.
3. The existing catch/persistence path (same `catch (err) { const {status,body}=mapTailorError(err); ... genState:'failed' ... }` pattern used for both /tailor and /letter) already sets `genState:'failed'` and leaves `current` untouched on any thrown error — verify a DecisionContractError flows through it correctly (it should, since it's just another thrown error mapped by mapTailorError).

INTEGRATION requirement (spec Phase 0): the proof must be that `tailor()` actually CALLS the validator — feed a genuinely contract-violating recorded/constructed fixture decision through the real pipeline (FixtureEngine -> tailor) and assert it throws `DecisionContractError`. Construct a violating fixture decision in-test (e.g. a decision that omits a library entry, or duplicates a rank within a section) — do NOT add a bad fixture file to `test/fixtures/decisions/` (that dir is sacred). Use a FixtureEngine pointed at a temp dir, or call tailor() with a stub engine that returns the violating decision.
tickets.acceptance:
- `bun run check` exit 0; `bun run build` exit 0; `bun run lint` exit 0; `bunx vitest run` FULL suite all pass (this is where fixture reconciliation is proven end-to-end — the keyless suite runs tailor() over real fixtures via FixtureEngine and must stay green).
- Integration test (extends `test/api.applications-tailor.test.ts` or a sibling), RED-TEAM-sharpened: a contract-violating decision driven through the REAL tailor() pipeline throws `DecisionContractError` (assert `err instanceof DecisionContractError` specifically, NOT just 'some error'). CRITICAL: the violation must be one `assemble()` does NOT already guard — assemble.ts:35 throws a plain `Error` on an unknown/foreign entryId, so a foreign-id case could be rescued by assemble and never reach the contract check. Use a DUPLICATE RANK WITHIN A SECTION, or an OMITTED-id partition violation where every id present IS known to assemble — proving the flat contract check fires BEFORE assemble and isn't swallowed. AND use a counting/spy engine: assert `engine.decide()` was called EXACTLY ONCE for a contract-invalid decision (proves the check runs in tailor()'s orchestration, not inside the provider's one-retry-on-any-error try/catch — no wasted second model call).
- Route/persistence test mirroring & extending RED-TEAM #11 (api.applications-tailor.test.ts:233): PIN the chosen HTTP code as a specific literal and assert it differs from EVERY code `mapTailorError` currently returns (422 no_fixture, 502 fabrication/provider_error, 401 key_invalid, 429 rate_limited) and error string !== 'fabrication'. Drive the app to genState 'tailored' via a prior SUCCESSFUL tailor first; capture that stored `current` as the baseline; then a contract-violating re-tailor → asserts the transition 'tailored' -> 'failed' (not a value checked in isolation) and the stored `current` deep-equals the captured baseline (before/after/before contrast, positive control included).
- No new fixture files under test/fixtures/decisions/.

tickets.title: Pure JD-signal coverage function reusing the flip-eval matcher via a client-safe shared module (+ keyless unit contrast tests)
tickets.context:
Depends on all of P0 (T002) being closed — the human confirmed contract-first de-risk order, and this coverage work reads the SAME assembled-resume/lede shape P0 just hardened. LOCKED (oracle.md): no LLM (pure mechanical function); no evaluative judgment (factual 'no lede addresses X' only); reuse the flip-eval matcher — do NOT write a fresh matcher; SYSTEM_PROMPT frozen.

THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT (why a shared module): the coverage readout must derive CLIENT-SIDE per render in ReasoningPanel (T004). The mandated-reuse matcher currently lives in `src/server/tailor/evalcore.ts` as MODULE-PRIVATE `rationaleReferencesSignal(rationale, signals)` and `tokenize(phrase)` — but evalcore.ts imports `node:crypto` and letter code, so it is SERVER-ONLY and cannot be imported by the client. So: EXTRACT the token-matching primitive into a NEW client-safe shared module `src/shared/signal-coverage.ts` (no `node:*` imports — like schema.ts/sections.ts/types, importable by both client and server), and have evalcore.ts IMPORT it instead of defining it locally (single source — the readout and flip-eval can NEVER drift on what 'references a signal' means). Keep evalcore.ts's PUBLIC exports (hashKey, CONTRAST_JDS, flipPredicate, tagShuffle, letter*) byte-unchanged in signature; only its internal matcher moves.

BUILD in `src/shared/signal-coverage.ts`:
1. `tokenize(phrase)` — moved verbatim from evalcore (lowercase, split on /[^a-z0-9]+/, filter Boolean).
2. A per-phrase matcher, e.g. `rationaleReferencesPhrase(rationale, phrase): boolean` = tokenize(phrase).some(tok => tok.length>=4 && rationale.toLowerCase().includes(tok)). This is the ANY-shared-≥4-char-token primitive — the DOCUMENTED LIMIT (two signals sharing a ≥4-char token can both read covered; accepted, disclosed).
3. `export function uncoveredSignals(resume: TailoredResume): string[]` — the coverage function. Candidate signals = resume.signals.weights ∪ resume.signals.hardRequirements folded into ONE set (roleLevel EXCLUDED). Collect every LEDE rationale = each group's `group.leadRationale` across resume.sections (assemble puts the lede's rationale there; items[0] is the lede). A signal is ADDRESSED iff SOME lede rationale references it via rationaleReferencesPhrase — NEVER a non-lede item's rationale, NEVER any item's `text`. uncovered = candidate signals referenced by NO lede rationale, in stable order (weights then hardRequirements, dedup preserving first occurrence). (The hide-when-empty and hide-when-zero-ledes SURFACE rules are T004's — this function just returns the uncovered array.)

Then refactor evalcore.ts's `rationaleReferencesSignal` to call the shared primitive over its candidate tokens (roleLevel + weights + hardRequirements) so flipPredicate behavior is UNCHANGED. Do NOT touch prompt.ts, assemble.ts, or the recorded fixtures.
tickets.acceptance:
- `bun run check` exit 0; `bun run build` exit 0 (proves NO node:* import leaked into the client bundle via the new shared module or ReasoningPanel's future import); `bun run lint` exit 0; `bunx vitest run` FULL suite all pass (evalcore/flip-eval tests including test/evalcore-letter.test.ts stay green — matcher behavior unchanged).
- NEW `test/signal-coverage.test.ts`, keyless, hand-built TailoredResume inputs, RED-TEAM-sharpened contrast cases (assert EXACT signal-string arrays, not cardinality):
  - weights=['platform SDK productization','API versioning'], one lede rationale naming platform/SDK -> uncovered=['API versioning']; add a second lede naming 'API versioning' -> uncovered=[].
  - a signal only in hardRequirements, named by no lede rationale -> in uncovered; named by a lede rationale -> not.
  - roleLevel exclusion: a resume whose roleLevel shares NO token with any lede rationale AND is not in weights/hardRequirements -> roleLevel never appears in uncoveredSignals output (asserts on output contents, proving exclusion).
  - lede-only, tightened: the SAME signal named by a NON-lede item's leadRationale AND by NO lede rationale in the same resume -> still uncovered (not two separate signals — a builder can't pass by testing an already-covered signal).
  - text-not-rationale, tightened: a signal token present VERBATIM in a lede item's `text` and in NO rationale anywhere -> still uncovered (fixture crafted so a text-fallback impl would flip it to covered).
  - dedup: the same phrase present in BOTH weights and hardRequirements -> appears EXACTLY ONCE in uncoveredSignals output.
  - documented-limit: two signals whose ONLY overlap is a single incidental >=4-char token (e.g. 'container orchestration' vs 'container deposit tracking' sharing only 'container'), one named by a lede rationale -> assert BOTH read covered (pins the matcher's looseness as intended, not genuine topical overlap).
- Single-source proof (RED-TEAM): (a) a grep/import assertion that evalcore.ts imports the matcher from `@shared/signal-coverage` and defines NO local `tokenize`/token-matcher of its own; AND (b) a differential test on a crafted input where the >=4-char looseness matters, asserting evalcore's `rationaleReferencesSignal` and the shared matcher agree (same code path, not a divergent copy).

tickets.title: Surface uncovered signals in ReasoningPanel with honest non-evaluative copy + applications-project e2e from real decision data
tickets.origin: spec Deliverable 2 (surface + honest framing + e2e) + Phase 1
tickets.context:
Depends on T003, which built `uncoveredSignals(resume): string[]` in `src/shared/signal-coverage.ts` (client-safe). LOCKED (oracle.md): extend the ReasoningPanel — do NOT rebuild it; keyless, always-on, derived PER RENDER; factual 'no lede addresses X' copy — NEVER 'your resume lacks X' or any good/bad judgment; reasoning strings never enter the PDF subtree (ReasoningPanel is already a sibling of DocumentPreview — safe).

`src/client/components/ReasoningPanel.tsx` (39 lines today) renders WeightBar(signals), per-group leadRationale Callouts, and CutList. BUILD ONLY THIS: add an 'uncovered signals' section that calls `uncoveredSignals(resume)` (import from `@shared/signal-coverage` — NOT an injected prop) and lists the uncovered signals under non-evaluative copy — literally phrased as 'no lede addresses …' (or equivalent that says no LEDE addresses it, never that the resume lacks it). HIDE the section when: (a) the uncovered set is empty, OR (b) the resume has ZERO ledes (no groups across sections — e.g. everything cut; otherwise every signal would falsely read uncovered as 'your resume lacks X'). Match the panel's existing className conventions (reasoning-panel__*). Do not add config knobs.

E2E: add `test/e2e/signal-coverage.spec.ts` to the `applications` playwright project — `signal-coverage` is NOT a new project, it is a spec added to the applications project's `testMatch` regex in `playwright.config.ts` (append `|signal-coverage`), or the project won't run it. Run it via `bunx playwright test --project=applications --grep signal-coverage`. Model it on existing applications specs (e.g. tap-targets.spec.ts, card-detail.spec.ts): import { login, createApplication, tailor } from './helpers/workspace' and CONTRAST_JDS from '../../src/server/tailor/evalcore'; drive a REAL tailored application (recorded fixture — CONTRAST_JDS[0] is the 'platform-sdk' scenario other specs reuse) to a detail route where ReasoningPanel renders, and assert against the DERIVED uncovered set (real decision data flowing through assemble -> uncoveredSignals), NOT an injected uncovered prop. The pinned fixture must yield >=1 covered AND >=1 uncovered signal — verify by inspection: platform-sdk has 5 weights and one lede rationale ('leads with direct experience designing and shipping a public-facing SDK…') that references some weights (e.g. 'public-facing', 'external') but not others (e.g. 'versioning'/'documentation') — confirm the actual split at build time and pick/assert accordingly. Assert: the uncovered signal renders under 'no lede addresses' copy; a covered signal is ABSENT from that list; and a case with an empty uncovered set (or zero ledes) does NOT render the section.

- `bunx playwright test --project=applications --grep signal-coverage` runs the NEW spec under the APPLICATIONS project specifically and it passes (the builder runs its own new gate-tier spec; the full applications gate runs at phase close).
